newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australis sees better year ahead.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australis sees better year ahead.

text.p: Australis Media Ltd chairman Mark Johnson said on Wednesday the pay tv operator was expecting a distinctly better year this year than last.
Australis reported a net loss of A$51.1 million for the first quarter to September 30 after a net loss of A$251.69 million in the year to June 1996.

Johnson, speaking at the annual meeting, said the company would file a registation with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission within a week or so for its previously announced US$150 million senior secured note issue.

Johnson also said Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd and Lenfest Communications Inc would be invited to nominate board members in recognition of their contribution to the Australis recapitalisation plan.
He said Australis had 98,000 subscribers as of November 30.
"Clearly the liquidity crisis has had considerable impact on consumer confidence and the company has to now rebuild and restore this," he said.
Johnson said Australis' combined debt and equity raising of US$250 million, together with anticipated cash inflows, were expected to finance it through to a positive cash flow position.
"This closes the financial liquidity crisis chapter and puts the company on a solid financial basis going forward," he said.
"The company has a clear strategy which takes account of its resources and the competitive state of the pay tv industry."

He said the satellite-based provider's cost base had been significantly reduced to accommodate a more targeted sales and marketing plan aimed primarily at subscribers in non-cable areas. "The quarterly results to 30 September 1996 show the positive impact of this approach," he said, noting the loss was A$10.8 million lower than that in the previous quarter.
"The focus on reducing costs and maximising efficiencies will continue," Johnson said.
Johnson said Australis was committed to the implementation of a DTH satellite joint venture with cable rival Optus Vision, scheduled to begin on July 1.
"Significant cost reductions and funding benefits are expected to flow to the company from the arrangements," he said.

After June, the number of channels which can be delivered via DTH transmissions will no longer be restricted. "The company will be introducing new products and ideas to increase the number of channels and the choice available to subscribers following further deregulation of the industry," Johnson said.
"The company has been refinanced and is making good progress in developing a focussed and disciplined business," he said.
"Important opportunities are open to us," he added.
"In particular, we believe that satellite has been under-estimated as a means of pay television delivery," he said.
Johnson said most Australian homes would not be passed by cable within the foreseeable future, "and many will never be passed by cable."
